title: Prompt Refinement Workshop (Lab)
summary: Teams iterate a weak prompt across several versions with a one-change-per-version log, then refine for clarity and accuracy together and justify a best-balanced version from their trade-off evidence.
objectives: Iterate a prompt across several versions to raise output quality, logging each change and its effect.
Refine for two goals at once (clarity and accuracy) and discuss the trade-off.

body: In the Core lesson you made one smart change to a prompt. Today you run a full workshop: version 1, 2, 3, maybe 4 - each a single change you can defend.
Then comes the real challenge of a designer: chasing two goals at once, clarity and accuracy, and discovering that helping one can cost the other. Your log will prove exactly what worked.

sections.heading: I can…
items: I can iterate a prompt across several versions and log each change and its effect.
I can refine for two goals at once and explain the trade-off between them.
I can use my log as evidence for which change helped the most.

terms.definition: To improve something step by step across several versions.
When improving one goal makes another goal worse.
The best compromise between competing goals for a purpose.
How correct and on-topic the output is.
How easy the output is to understand.

sections.heading: Iterate and keep the receipts
body: A designer does not stop at the first improvement. You [[iterate]] - version by version - changing one thing each time and logging its effect.
The log is your **evidence**. When someone asks which change helped most, you point to the row that proves it, because you changed only one thing that version.

sections.heading: Two goals, one trade-off
body: Now aim for two goals at once: [[clarity]] and [[accuracy]]. Sometimes a change that makes the output clearer quietly drops an accurate detail.
That is a [[trade-off]]. Your job is not to pretend it away but to choose the version that best balances both goals for your purpose - and to say why.

sections.label: Let's try it - hands-on
sections.heading: Let's try it - hands-on
body: Your team iterates a weak prompt across several versions, logging each change and effect, then balances clarity and accuracy and chooses the best version with evidence.
items: Set the goal and judge the v1 output.
Make v2 with one change; log the reason and revealed effect.
Iterate to v3 and v4, one change each, logging cause and effect.
Add accuracy as a second goal alongside clarity.
Find and record a trade-off where one goal cost the other.
Choose the best-balanced version and justify it from your log.

sections.heading: Think about it
items: Which single change gave the biggest quality jump, and how does your log prove it?
Where did clarity and accuracy pull against each other, and how did you decide?

sections.heading: My reflection
items: Write the best-balanced version your team chose and one sentence on why.
Explain what balancing two goals taught you about making design decisions.

worksheet.title: Week 2 - Lab - Worksheet | Prompt Refinement Workshop (Lab)

questions.prompt: A team iterates a prompt from v1 to v4. Because v4 is the newest version, it must be the team's best-balanced version.

feedback.correct: Right - a later change can cost you on one goal, so the best balance is the version your log shows fits the purpose, not simply the last one.
feedback.incorrect: Each version changes one thing, and a change can help clarity while hurting accuracy - so v4 is best only if the log shows it balances both goals for your purpose.

questions.prompt:
A team iterated a notice about the school recycling drive, one change per version, and scored each output out of 5 for clarity and accuracy.
v1 "Write about the recycling drive." - clarity 2, accuracy 3
v2 added "write it in 4 sentences" - clarity 4, accuracy 3
v3 added "for Grade 3 readers" - clarity 5, accuracy 1 (the collection dates disappeared)
v4 added "include the collection dates" - clarity 4, accuracy 4
Match each version with what its log entry shows.

right.text: Brought a true detail back, costing a little clarity.
Made the notice clearer and left accuracy exactly as it was.
The starting point, with nothing yet to compare it against.
Gave the clearest output of all, but a true detail was lost.

feedback.correct: Because only one thing changed each time, every row of the log can be read as the cause of that version's effect.
feedback.incorrect: Compare each version's two scores with the version before it: that difference is the effect of the one change made in that version.

questions.prompt: Using the same log (v1 clarity 2 / accuracy 3; v2 clarity 4 / accuracy 3; v3 clarity 5 / accuracy 1; v4 clarity 4 / accuracy 4): v3’s accuracy score is how many points lower than v2’s?

feedback.correct: Accuracy fell from 3 to 1, so the clearer v3 cost 2 accuracy points - that number is the size of the trade-off.
feedback.incorrect: Subtract v3's accuracy score from v2's: 3 - 1 = 2. Measuring the loss is how you show a trade-off with evidence instead of just claiming one.

questions.prompt: Using the same log (v1 clarity 2 / accuracy 3; v2 clarity 4 / accuracy 3; v3 clarity 5 / accuracy 1, dates dropped; v4 clarity 4 / accuracy 4), which statements does the log actually support? Choose all that apply.

options.text: v2's change raised clarity without changing accuracy.
v3's change raised clarity but lowered accuracy.
v4 is the only version scoring 4 or more on both goals.
Every version after v1 improved both goals.
v3 lost accuracy because the team changed two things in that version.

feedback.correct: You read the log as evidence: two of the changes helped one goal only, and just one version reaches 4 on both.
feedback.incorrect: Check each claim against the numbers - v3's accuracy fell, so not every version improved both goals, and the log records only one change per version.

questions.prompt: The notice will be handed to Grade 3 students and it must tell them the correct collection dates. Using the same log (v1 clarity 2 / accuracy 3; v2 clarity 4 / accuracy 3; v3 clarity 5 / accuracy 1, dates dropped; v4 clarity 4 / accuracy 4), which choice of best-balanced version is best justified by the evidence?

options.text: v4, because it keeps clarity high at 4 while bringing the correct dates back.
v3, because it scored highest of all the versions on clarity.
v2, because it was the first version that improved on v1.
v1, because it was written before any goal pulled against another.

feedback.correct: The purpose needs both goals, and v4 is the only version the log shows meeting both - a clear notice that still carries the right dates.
feedback.incorrect: Judge against the purpose: a notice missing the collection dates fails its job however clear it reads, so the highest clarity score alone cannot justify the choice.

formative.targets: Grade 5 Advanced: refines prompts to improve output quality and explains why
formative.check: Iteration log across several versions plus a two-goal trade-off justification
formative.successCriteria: Iterates a prompt with a reasoned log and chooses a best-balanced version, explaining the trade-off with evidence.
formative.evidence: Multi-version refinement log with trade-off note.
